source.method: chapter titles from each book's Contents page; topics from each chapter PDF's numbered section and subsection headings (Introduction, Summary, Miscellaneous Examples and Exercises are not topics; small neighbouring subsections are grouped; long sections with no subsections are split by the definitions, theorems or integral types the section itself lists, keeping the section heading in the topic title; the appendices Proofs in Mathematics and Mathematical Modelling and the Supplementary Material are not chapters and are not included)

topics.title: Types of Relations: Empty, Universal, Reflexive, Symmetric and Transitive
objectives: Student can define a relation in a set A as a subset of A x A and identify empty and universal relations
Student can test whether a relation is reflexive, symmetric or transitive
visualIdeas: arrow diagram of a relation on a small set

topics.title: Types of Relations: Equivalence Relations and Equivalence Classes
objectives: Student can prove that a relation is an equivalence relation, as for congruence modulo n or parallel lines
Student can find equivalence classes and explain how an equivalence relation partitions a set into disjoint subsets
visualIdeas: integers split into the even class [0] and the odd class [1]

topics.title: Types of Functions: One-one and Onto Functions
objectives: Student can define one-one (injective), many-one and onto (surjective) functions
Student can prove whether a given function is one-one and whether it is onto
Student can define and identify bijective functions
visualIdeas: arrow diagrams of one-one, onto, both and neither

topics.title: Composition of Functions and Invertible Function
objectives: Student can find the composition g o f of two functions and its domain
Student can define an invertible function and state that f is invertible exactly when it is one-one and onto
Student can find the inverse of an invertible function
visualIdeas: function machines f then g chained
f and its inverse mapping back

topics.title: Basic Concepts: Inverse Sine and Inverse Cosine Functions
objectives: Student can restrict the domain of sine and cosine to make them one-one and onto and define sin^-1 and cos^-1
Student can state the domain, principal value branch and graph of sin^-1 x and cos^-1 x
visualIdeas: graph of y = sin x with the principal branch highlighted and its reflection in y = x

topics.title: Basic Concepts: Inverse Cosecant, Secant, Tangent and Cotangent Functions
objectives: Student can define cosec^-1, sec^-1, tan^-1 and cot^-1 with their domains and principal value branches
Student can sketch the graphs of these inverse functions
visualIdeas: table of the six inverse trigonometric functions with domains and ranges

topics.title: Basic Concepts: Principal Values
objectives: Student can find the principal value of expressions such as sin^-1(1/2) and cos^-1(-1/2)
Student can evaluate expressions combining inverse trigonometric functions using their principal branches
visualIdeas: unit circle with principal value arcs marked

topics.title: Properties of Inverse Trigonometric Functions
objectives: Student can use sin(sin^-1 x) = x and sin^-1(sin x) = x within the principal branches
Student can simplify expressions with inverse trigonometric functions by a suitable substitution, such as x = sin theta
Student can prove identities such as sin^-1(2x sqrt(1 - x^2)) = 2 sin^-1 x on the stated interval
visualIdeas: substitution x = tan theta turning an expression into theta

topics.title: Matrix and Order of a Matrix
objectives: Student can define a matrix as a rectangular array and identify its elements a_ij
Student can state the order m x n of a matrix and construct a matrix from a rule for a_ij
Student can represent real data, such as items held by people, as a matrix
visualIdeas: 2 x 3 matrix with rows and columns labelled

topics.title: Types of Matrices
objectives: Student can identify column, row, square, diagonal, scalar, identity and zero matrices
Student can give examples of each type of matrix
visualIdeas: gallery of matrix types with their patterns highlighted

topics.title: Equality of Matrices
objectives: Student can state when two matrices are equal
Student can find unknowns by equating corresponding elements of equal matrices
visualIdeas: two matrices with corresponding entries joined by lines

topics.title: Addition of Matrices
objectives: Student can add two matrices of the same order element by element
Student can explain why matrices of different orders cannot be added
visualIdeas: two production tables from factories added cell by cell

topics.title: Multiplication of a Matrix by a Scalar
objectives: Student can multiply a matrix by a scalar
Student can find the negative of a matrix and the difference of two matrices
visualIdeas: each entry of a matrix doubled

topics.title: Properties of Matrix Addition and Scalar Multiplication
objectives: Student can state and use the commutative, associative, identity and inverse properties of matrix addition
Student can use the properties k(A + B) = kA + kB and (k + l)A = kA + lA
visualIdeas: A + B and B + A computed side by side

topics.title: Multiplication of Matrices
objectives: Student can state the condition for the product AB to be defined and its order
Student can multiply two matrices row by column
Student can show with an example that AB need not equal BA and that AB = O does not mean A = O or B = O
visualIdeas: row of A sliding along a column of B to give one entry of AB

topics.title: Properties of Multiplication of Matrices
objectives: Student can use the associative and distributive laws of matrix multiplication
Student can use the identity matrix as the multiplicative identity
Student can verify identities such as A^2 - 5A + 7I = O for a given matrix
visualIdeas: (AB)C and A(BC) computed and compared

topics.title: Transpose of a Matrix
objectives: Student can find the transpose of a matrix
Student can use the properties (A')' = A, (kA)' = kA', (A + B)' = A' + B' and (AB)' = B'A'
visualIdeas: rows of a matrix turned into columns

topics.title: Symmetric and Skew Symmetric Matrices
objectives: Student can identify symmetric (A' = A) and skew symmetric (A' = -A) matrices
Student can show that the diagonal elements of a skew symmetric matrix are zero
Student can express a square matrix as the sum of a symmetric and a skew symmetric matrix
visualIdeas: matrix mirrored about its leading diagonal

topics.title: Invertible Matrices
objectives: Student can define the inverse of a square matrix
Student can prove that the inverse of a matrix, if it exists, is unique and that (AB)^-1 = B^-1 A^-1
visualIdeas: A times its inverse giving the identity matrix

topics.title: Determinant of a Matrix of Order One and Two
objectives: Student can explain that every square matrix has a determinant, a number
Student can evaluate determinants of order one and two
visualIdeas: 2 x 2 determinant with the cross-multiplication pattern

topics.title: Determinant of a Matrix of Order 3 x 3
objectives: Student can expand a 3 x 3 determinant along any row or column
Student can choose the row or column with most zeros to simplify expansion
Student can use the fact that |kA| = k^n |A| for a square matrix of order n
visualIdeas: 3 x 3 determinant expanded along the first row with signs

topics.title: Area of a Triangle
objectives: Student can find the area of a triangle with given vertices using a determinant
Student can use the determinant to test collinearity of three points and find the equation of a line
visualIdeas: triangle on coordinate axes with its vertices in a determinant

topics.title: Minors and Cofactors
objectives: Student can find the minor and cofactor of an element of a determinant
Student can expand a determinant as the sum of products of elements and their cofactors
Student can show that elements multiplied by the cofactors of another row give zero
visualIdeas: 3 x 3 determinant with a row and column struck out to show a minor

topics.title: Adjoint of a Matrix
objectives: Student can find the adjoint of a square matrix as the transpose of the cofactor matrix
Student can use the theorem A(adj A) = (adj A)A = |A| I
visualIdeas: cofactor matrix transposed into the adjoint

topics.title: Adjoint and Inverse of a Matrix: Inverse of a Matrix
objectives: Student can distinguish singular and non-singular matrices
Student can state that a square matrix is invertible if and only if it is non-singular
Student can find the inverse of a matrix using A^-1 = (1/|A|) adj A
visualIdeas: flow chart: find |A|, then adj A, then divide

topics.title: Solution of System of Linear Equations using Inverse of a Matrix
objectives: Student can define consistent and inconsistent systems of equations
Student can write a system of linear equations as AX = B and solve it by X = A^-1 B when |A| is not zero
Student can decide when |A| = 0 whether the system has no solution or infinitely many using (adj A)B
visualIdeas: three equations rewritten as one matrix equation AX = B

topics.title: Continuity
objectives: Student can define continuity of a real function at a point using left-hand limit, right-hand limit and value
Student can define a continuous function and check continuity of functions such as |x|, polynomials and piecewise functions
Student can find points of discontinuity of a given function
visualIdeas: graph with a jump at x = c beside a smooth graph

topics.title: Algebra of Continuous Functions
objectives: Student can state that sums, differences, products and quotients of continuous functions are continuous
Student can use the theorem that a composition of continuous functions is continuous
visualIdeas: two continuous graphs and their sum

topics.title: Differentiability
objectives: Student can define the derivative of a function at a point and differentiability on an interval
Student can prove that a differentiable function is continuous and show by |x| that the converse is false
visualIdeas: corner of y = |x| at the origin

topics.title: Derivatives of Composite Functions
objectives: Student can state and apply the chain rule to differentiate composite functions
Student can differentiate functions such as sin(x^2) and (2x + 3)^n

objectives: Student can distinguish explicit and implicit functions
Student can find dy/dx by differentiating an implicit relation term by term
visualIdeas: circle x^2 + y^2 = r^2 with a tangent slope

topics.title: Derivatives of Inverse Trigonometric Functions
objectives: Student can derive the derivatives of sin^-1 x and cos^-1 x and tan^-1 x
Student can use the table of derivatives of inverse trigonometric functions
visualIdeas: table of the six derivatives

topics.title: Exponential and Logarithmic Functions
objectives: Student can define the exponential function b^x and the logarithm function and describe their graphs
Student can state properties of logarithms and the derivatives of e^x and log x
visualIdeas: graphs of y = e^x and y = log x reflected in y = x

topics.title: Logarithmic Differentiation
objectives: Student can use logarithmic differentiation for functions of the form [u(x)]^v(x)
Student can differentiate long products and quotients by taking logarithms first
visualIdeas: x^x rewritten as e^(x log x)

topics.title: Derivatives of Functions in Parametric Forms
objectives: Student can find dy/dx when x and y are given in terms of a parameter t
Student can apply the method to curves such as x = a cos t, y = a sin t
visualIdeas: point moving on a circle as t varies

topics.title: Second Order Derivative
objectives: Student can find the second order derivative of a function
Student can verify relations such as y'' + y = 0 for given functions
visualIdeas: graph with slope and change of slope shown

topics.title: Rate of Change of Quantities
objectives: Student can interpret dy/dx as the rate of change of y with respect to x

topics.title: Increasing and Decreasing Functions

Student can use the sign of the derivative to test whether a function is increasing or decreasing
Student can find the intervals in which a function is increasing or decreasing
visualIdeas: graph rising and falling with tangent slopes marked positive and negative

topics.title: Maxima and Minima: Local Maxima, Local Minima and the First Derivative Test
objectives: Student can define maximum, minimum, local maximum and local minimum values
Student can find critical points and use the first derivative test to classify them
visualIdeas: graph with peaks and valleys and horizontal tangents

topics.title: Maxima and Minima: Second Derivative Test
objectives: Student can apply the second derivative test to find local maxima and minima
Student can recognise when the second derivative test fails and return to the first derivative test
Student can solve applied problems such as two positive numbers with a given sum, the shortest distance from a point to a parabola, or the trapezium of greatest area
visualIdeas: concave up and concave down curves at critical points

topics.title: Maximum and Minimum Values of a Function in a Closed Interval
objectives: Student can find absolute maximum and minimum values of a function on a closed interval
Student can solve problems such as finding the nearest distance between a fixed point and a body moving along a curve

topics.title: Integration as an Inverse Process of Differentiation
objectives: Student can define an antiderivative (primitive) and the indefinite integral with an arbitrary constant
Student can list the standard integrals that follow from known derivatives
Student can interpret the constant of integration as a family of curves
visualIdeas: family of parallel curves y = x^2 + C

topics.title: Some Properties of Indefinite Integral
objectives: Student can use the properties that integration and differentiation are inverse processes
Student can integrate sums and constant multiples of functions term by term

topics.title: Integration by Substitution

objectives: Student can use identities to rewrite powers such as sin^2 x, cos^2 x and sin^3 x in integrable form

topics.title: Integration by Parts

Student can choose the first function sensibly, as in integrals of x cos x, log x and x e^x

topics.title: Integral of the Type e^x [f(x) + f'(x)] dx

topics.title: Integrals of Some More Types

topics.title: Definite Integral
objectives: Student can write the definite integral of f from a to b and identify its lower and upper limits

topics.title: Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
objectives: Student can define the area function A(x) as the integral of f from a to x

topics.title: Evaluation of Definite Integrals by Substitution
objectives: Student can evaluate definite integrals by substitution, changing the limits to the new variable
Student can explain why, after changing the limits, there is no need to return to the original variable

topics.title: Some Properties of Definite Integrals
objectives: Student can state and prove the properties P0 to P7 of definite integrals
Student can use properties such as the integral of f(x) equals the integral of f(a - x) to evaluate integrals

curve crossing the x-axis with areas A1 and A2
